##  Understanding Sea Ice Thickness

Sea ice thickness refers to how deep a sheet of frozen ocean water is --
from its surface down to where it meets the open water below.   

While sea ice extent tells you how much area is covered by ice, **sea ice thickness** tells 
you how much ice there actually is, and how tough or long-lasting it's likely to be.


## Not all sea ice is the same

Sea ice thickness can be categorized commonly as first-year ice and multi-year ice.  
First year ice is relatively thin and forms over a single winter whereas multi-year ice
has survived one or more seasons, building over time; multi-year ice can be several meters thick
and generally harder.
